name: Sarah H. Wu
title: PhD student in Media Psychology
bio: Through my research, I aim to identify and address situations where technology has the potential to undermine human capacities. Some broad questions I explore include: What are the long-term consequences of using chatbots to navigate social situations? How can we provide helpful content recommendations for today's parents, whose children are growing up in an algorithmically curated media environment?

Before starting my PhD, I earned my BA in Psychology from Reed College in Portland, OR, and I was a predoctoral research fellow at the Stanford Institute for Research in the Social Sciences (IRiSS) and the Stanford Social Media Lab.

Outside of research, I play violin semi-professionally in Argentine tango ensembles across the Bay Area. I also volunteer for the Peninsula Symphony through their school outreach program, which brings live music to students in underserved communities.
